pairs.registryProposal: canvas-graph's golden path names the read-only-renderer off-ramp ('if nobody ever drags a node you need a renderer, and layout becomes a pure function') but then hands off to six techniques all written for the editor case, so a renderer-shaped context has to re-derive which clauses still bind. Add a stage: read-only-renderer precondition marker stating explicitly what survives it - layout determinism including tie-breaking, rung-3 memoization on the hover path, shared node/edge anchor geometry and arrowhead placement, focus-context economy, and the entire accessibility model - and what it genuinely retires: provenance, layout persistence/migration, placement policy, drag/connect/snap/marquee, and (when the diagram is fit to its container) the transform authority itself. Without that marker, not-applicable is available as a blanket excuse for four of six techniques on a shape common enough to deserve its own stage.

pairs.subject: scheduling
pairs.evidence: src/features/schedules/components/EventTooltip.tsx:6 - the only component that explains a calendar fire (exact time, kind, the unverified_tooltip reason text, overlap partners) is imported by nothing, so the calendar's non-fire disclosure renders as an unlabeled dashed chip and 'why didn't this fire?' is unanswerable on the surface built to answer it.

techniques.evidence: src/features/schedules/libs/useCronPreview.ts:105-112 delegates every cron projection to the engine's cron_fire_times_in_range seeded with agent.trigger_id (matching the engine's seed_hash H-token spread - seeded by identity, not random jitter); calendarHelpers.ts:82-91 records the deliberate deletion of the client-side cron parser whose step semantics drifted from the engine, useCronPreview.ts:216-234 mirrors interval phase off the engine-owned next_trigger_at anchor and returns nothing rather than inventing one when the anchor is null, and useScheduleActions.ts:112-119 omits next_trigger_at on a rule edit so the backend recomputes it in the same write.

src/features/schedules/components/ScheduleRow.tsx:360-386 surfaces the downtime gap explicitly as a per-trigger 'missed N while offline' banner with a bounded one-click backfill and a dismiss, BackfillModal.tsx:160-179 discloses the cap (lastResult.capped) and the exact replayed slot times, and useScheduleActions.ts:76-91 read-modify-writes the trigger config so a frequency edit never wipes the per-item max_backfill policy; calendarHelpers.ts:326-332 further refuses to bind a backfilled run (stamped at backfill time, not its due time) to a nominal slot.

The technique's one UI-facing clause - 'reentrancy includes the humans; the manual run-now affordance passes through the same dispatch guard' - is met at src/features/schedules/components/ScheduleRow.tsx:236-247, where Play is disabled while isExecuting and delegates to useScheduleActions.ts:42-59, which calls the engine's executePersona(persona_id, trigger_id) rather than any UI-side firing path; claims, reapers, atomic release and the generation counter are scheduler-runtime clauses realized in the Rust engine, not expressible here.

Failing precondition: the technique governs routing a published event against a subscription set, and nothing in this context publishes, subscribes or filters - ScheduleEntry is derived solely from clock-family fields (src/features/schedules/libs/scheduleHelpers.ts:37-42: cron_expression / interval_seconds), the CronAgent binding carries no event kind or filter, and the subscription surface (getSubscriptionHealth, src/api/pipeline/scheduler.ts:21) belongs to a different context.

Failing precondition: all four suppression shapes are decisions made and persisted by the evaluator/dispatcher, and no file here evaluates a condition, chooses a suppression key or holds a window - the schedules IPC contract (CronAgent, ScheduleMissedRuns) exposes no cooldown or suppressed-count field for this surface to render; the technique's one UI clause is realized on the trigger status surface in a sibling context at src/features/triggers/sub_triggers/RateLimitControls.tsx:148-152, and useScheduleActions.ts:79-80 is careful to preserve rate_limit on edit rather than owning it.

src/features/schedules/components/EventTooltip.tsx:6 should be the calendar's per-fire disclosure but is imported by no file in the repo, and the block that does render (EventBlock.tsx:42-54, mounted at WeekView.tsx:113-123 and MonthView.tsx:92-102) carries no title or hover surface - so a past-unknown slot, precisely this technique's non-fire signal, shows an agent name and a grey question mark with no time, no reason and no access to the unverified_tooltip text written for it, and in month view even the fire's clock time is unreadable; the forward ledger (ScheduleRow.tsx:195-213) and the downtime reason badges (ScheduleRow.tsx:159-166) are otherwise well realized.

pairs.registryProposal: schedule-observability names four surfaces but is written entirely from the decider's side: it never states that the run and non-fire ledgers must be QUERYABLE by the display layer, which is where this pair actually fails. The engine here writes rich non-fire reasons (schedule.skipped.overlap with reason previous_run_active, stuck_reclaimed, budget/window declines) yet the read contract this UI is given (list_recent_schedule_runs returns real runs only; PersonaExecution has trigger_id but no cause and no represented due time; ScheduleMissedRuns covers only offline gaps) forces the calendar to collapse every declined occurrence into one undifferentiated past-unknown. Proposal: add a decision rule that the non-fire ledger must be exposed as a queryable read model carrying the same reason tokens the decider wrote, and that a run record must carry its cause and represented due time across the API boundary - plus a react--schedule-observability application teaching the honest-display pattern this repo already half-invented (matchPastSlotsToRuns and past-unknown as a refusal to assert, calendarHelpers.ts:283-332).

pairs.subject: docs-sync
pairs.evidence: doc_rot.rs is a strong rot detector (unverifiable as a first-class verdict, priority-ordered stable truncation), but the coupling around it is only ever validated in the map-to-disk direction and only ever collected by a 6-hour-throttled scan (src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/doc_rot.rs:106, context_audit.rs:56) - so what the maps omit, and what the declared tour/marketing surfaces owe, is invisible by construction.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/context_audit.rs:56-70 - the standing audit's totals count dangling paths, overlaps and unresolved cross-refs (map to disk) but never the inverse, and the only source-side coverage fraction is computed transiently inside a scan run (context_generation.rs:1762), so between scans a map covering a shrinking share of the tree still reports 'within policy'; separately doc_rot.rs:317-321 silently filters out doc-map entries whose doc file is gone instead of reporting the dead entry.

src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/doc_rot.rs:104-106 (RESCAN_MIN_HOURS) - the in-app collector is a throttled periodic scan and git is read only as git log history (doc_rot.rs:169), never as a diff at a change boundary, and doc_status has no dismissed state (doc_rot.rs:671-699), so debt is collected after context has evaporated and the dismissal rate is structurally unknowable.

src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/doc_rot.rs:374-392 - parse_doc_map reads only doc and sourceGlobs while the manifest it parses declares onboardingFlows on 17 of 37 entries and marketingModule on 24 (plus a 39-key flow registry), so the tour and marketing surfaces a change owes are enumerated in data and checked by nothing live in this context.

src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/doc_rot.rs:29-40 - the correction anatomy is otherwise strong (false claim kept visible, measurement with predicate, instrument named: '0 of 37 doc-map-managed docs were reachable'), but only 3 dated stamps exist across the ~10k lines judged (workspace_harvest.rs:69, workspace_verify.rs:48, context_generation.rs:1483), so these standing claims cannot be ordered, expired, or fed to the expired-claims rot signal.

src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/doc_rot.rs:732-742 doc_status_label ranks broken above stale above unverifiable above clean with unverifiable never collapsed into clean (pinned by the test at doc_rot.rs:877-886), over a declared-map-then-colocation-then-honesty ladder (doc_rot.rs:11-18, 649-653), dead-reference signals beyond timestamps (doc_rot.rs:463-532) and a priority-ordered, stably-truncated budget (doc_rot.rs:312-341, test 1061-1076).

src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/workspace_harvest.rs:231-241 - the per-scope ledger carries the anchor (last_harvested_at), what was covered (estimated_pct, run_count) and the consciously-skipped list carried into the next pass (unread_pockets), with unmeasured depth treated as owing rather than done (workspace_harvest.rs:144-146, 673); and context_generation.rs:1259-1265 refuses loudly when the range record is missing instead of silently defaulting to a full rewrite.

Precondition fails: the technique is stage multi-service and its own 'when not to reach for this' excludes single-tree coupling - every doc this context judges is coupled to source under the same project root (src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/doc_rot.rs:625-654 resolves scope prefixes against one root), and no document here carries a watch set or review date over another repository's history.

Precondition fails: no documentation registry lives in application source needing an out-of-band reader - the coupling manifest is a plain JSON file read with serde_json and no build (src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/doc_rot.rs:355-396), and the typed doc/context records are read straight from SQLite by in-process code (context_audit.rs:379-386).

src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/standards_scan.rs:367-375 - a timed-out run that parsed any findings returns Ok(count) with no comparison against the 20 rule keys compiled in from standards_ruleset.md, so a scan that assessed 4 of 20 rules reports '4 rules assessed' indistinguishably from a complete pass (and norm() at :79 silently refiles unlisted categories, as its own comment at :31-34 admits); doc_rot.rs:112-127 and workspace_verify.rs:546-568 show the project already knows how to do this.

src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/workspace_verify.rs:546-559 reconciles selected against checked and leaves lost practices unverified for re-selection, and src-tauri/db/src/repos/workspaces/adoption.rs:146,151-153 advances last_verified_at only on a landed 'adopted' verdict, with three resolutions (adopted/diverged/na) at adoption.rs:79-91; the evidence revision is recorded for the exported map at context_map_export.rs:239,251-254.

src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/context_generation.rs:1219-1231 - the delta no-op returns before prune_dangling_file_paths (:1825), prune_unresolvable_references (:1832) and report_context_audit (:1873), so on a quiet run the claim-binding walk never runs and work an earlier run deferred belongs to no subsequent diff; and the payload handed to the worker already standing in the repo (context_map_export.rs:352-395) carries no outstanding staleness, so rot measured as being consumed (doc_rot.rs:151-153 dirty_reads_30d) is never resolved by the session consuming it.

pairs.registryProposal: doc-rot-detection's verdict vocabulary should gain 'broken' as a fourth rung ranked ABOVE stale and unverifiable, not folded into stale as a mere dead-references signal. This implementation's measured argument (src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/doc_rot.rs:20-27, 732-742, test 889-924): a doc whose every reference has been renamed away couples to nothing, so it lands in the unverifiable population and nobody looks - the content signal is the ONLY verdict available for exactly the highest-risk documents, and it is mechanically checkable with near-perfect precision once guarded against truncated tokens (doc_rot.rs:412-459). Ranking it above the coupling-derived rungs is what closes the compounding blind spot the technique names but does not price. Note also that this bundle appears to have been forged from this very repo: scripts/docs/feature-doc-map.json matches the technique's measured counter-examples exactly (37 entries, 17 with flows, 24 with a marketing module, a 39-key flow registry), so these verdicts carry less independent evidential weight than a cross-repo backtest would.
